fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"The Golden Thread of Baal","body":"Chance Garton opens with an infographic he calls the golden thread of Baal, a key to what he terms the ancient ecclesiastical feudal system, the church hierarchy that governs the governors. The thread runs through bull, ox and cow symbolism and through any word built on B and L, since B trades with V, P and F while L drifts to R or N, letting bell, bull, bail, bill and Baal read as one family. Dylan Saccoccio adds the Phoenician capitals Tyre and Byblos, tzur meaning rock, lord and god, and Adonis, the dying and rising god of spring whose name simply means Lord."},{"title":"Limitless Fire and the Bill","body":"The Greek pyr means fire, and Chance argues that the familiar P to B and R to L shifts fold it back into Baal, so pyramid reads as limitless fire, which he ties to the pyramid added to the back of the dollar bill in 1935 as money became limitless fiat debt. Dylan links par and pharos to the towers of Sardinia and the Pictish brochs, at once fortresses, temples and lighthouses. Since faro is a lighthouse and farro is grain, Chance calls Pharaoh the bull lord of the grain whose fire guides, while the bull sacrificed to settle a debt becomes the bail a prisoner pays."},{"title":"Baal Peor Becomes Balfour","body":"Reading Numbers 25 aloud, Chance stresses the heads hung before the sun and the twenty four thousand dead, calling the chapter atrocity propaganda parked in front of something the compilers preferred hidden, and noting that plaga once meant to strike or wound before the Vulgate made it mass death. Dylan checks the Hebrew and finds Peor spelled with a vav, closer to pur, fire, and par, bull. Both then reach the Balfour Declaration of November 2, 1917, Arthur James Balfour writing to Lord Lionel Walter Rothschild, and Dylan contends that Semite is a category invented around 1800, with Porphyry calling Israel a Phoenician name for Kronos."},{"title":"The Irish Phoenician Trail","body":"Turning to the Celts, Chance holds that Celt and Gaul name one people through a C and G swap, and that the Phoenicians of the record are the Etruscans, Tyrrhenians and Pelasgians of the Italian peninsula rather than Levantine migrants. Dylan offers cel or kil as stone, the root behind church and behind the standing circles, so that asking whether someone had been to the stones meant asking whether they had been to church. The two read Charles Vallancey, who published in the early 1800s that the chief deity of the heathen Irish was Baal the sun, with May named the month of Baal's fire."},{"title":"Bellanus and the Beltane Fires","body":"Encyclopedia Britannica gives Bellanus one paragraph, possibly Bright One, tied to pastoralism and to the May 1 fire festival, yet denies he was a sun god, a hedge both hosts treat as deliberate suppression, while Wikipedia centers him on Aquileia in northeast Italy, identifies him with Apollo and links him to healing springs. Dylan reads the suffix nous as mind, making Bellanus a double of Dionysus. Chance then walks the same rite through Walpurgisnacht on April 30 and its saint, through the maypole, through the Balkan Yarilo and the twelfth century Yarovit, and through the Persian Chaharshanbe Suri that he sets beside Ash Wednesday."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: THE EMPIRE OF BAAL continues. This episode follows the golden thread westward into Celtic Europe, tracing the bull god's fingerprints across Ireland and Britain.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: What do Celtic mythology, Beltane, and the ancient Phoenicians have in common? In Part 2 of The Empire of Baal, Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio follow the linguistic and ritual signature of the bull god Baal across the ancient world, from the Mediterranean into Gaul, Britain, and Ireland, tracing a continuous system of ancient religion preserved across thousands of years and thousands of miles. Topics include the Celtic god Belenus and his philological identity with Dionysus, the shared origin of Beltane, Walpurgisnacht, and Ash Wednesday as fire festivals, the linguistic parallel between ancient Phoenician and Irish, the etymology of Pharaoh, pyramid, and Baal, the bull and Taurus symbolism throughout the Old Testament, and the gods Adonis, Bacchus, and Mithras as regional expressions of one ancient system. The members' half is jam packed, including the Baal connection to Sibyls, government, and the technological surveillance state. This is where Baal jumps out of history and reveals its ubiquity in our modern society.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Coins, Kings, and Manufactured Antiquity", "body": "The exclusive hour opens on the Cunobelinus coins of pre Roman Britain, where the mainstream sees a historical king and the hosts see a god. Bulls, a club wielding Hercules, a bull being sacrificed, even Janus faces, nearly everything in astrotheology turns up somewhere on this coinage. The only literary witness to the king is Suetonius, whose work survives solely as monkish copies made in the Middle Ages. Reading a sixteen hundreds antiquarian, they argue Cuno was a priestly title, so a coin stamped Cunobelinus may simply mean approved by the priesthood of Bel."}, {"title": "The Lateran and the Bulls of the Hidden Ones", "body": "Dylan turns to Saint John Lateran, where the papal bulls are signed, and unpacks lateo, the Latin root meaning to live in concealment, to escape notice, to lie hidden or lurk. Add the suffix ana and Lateran becomes the place of hidden ones. Latrea, the Greek word for worship and cult, sits right beside it, so the church and palace joined at that site read as a secret family issuing decrees. The bulls themselves come from bule or vuli, a council, plan, intention or determination, the perfect word for a secret order's undertakings."}, {"title": "From Oracle to Panopticon", "body": "The core of the exclusive hour is the sibyl. Because the Greek beta carries a V sound, sivula is simply civil, and kybernao, to steer or pilot, gives us both govern and cyber. Powerful men brought their intentions to the oracle, were steered by whatever answer came back, and left their secrets in the hands of the cult that ran her. Priests and confessionals continued the arrangement, and modern surveillance completes it. Information gathering used to steer or blackmail the course of civilization is not a product of the technological age but a project thousands of years old."}, {"title": "Virgil, the Cumaean Sibyl, and the Promised Golden Age", "body": "Virgil's fourth Eclogue announces the return of the virgin, the reign of Saturn and a golden race springing up throughout the world, and church fathers such as Lactantius and Augustine cited that pagan prophecy as testimony to Christ before his birth. Jerome rejected it, which the hosts read as proof the idea was widespread enough to require a rebuttal. Whether Virgil was real or the passage was forged later hardly matters, since establishments from the fourth century through the Renaissance invented documents from antiquity to prop up current dogma, and every generation since has been promised an imminent golden age."}, {"title": "Rabble, Robots, and the Eternal Now", "body": "The close turns personal. Rabble is labor reversed, robot descends from the Slavic rabu meaning slave, and robota means forced labor and servitude, so the whole feudal machine runs on making people predictable enough that the majority works for the minority. Against that, Chance offers a mystical counterweight, that cosmology is not a story about a beginning and an end but about the world being born anew in every moment, with no past and no future, only the eternal now. Liars pervert that feeling into chronology and prophecy, harvesting the attention people surrender when they check out of the present."}]
